newsitem.title: USA: U.S. DOE still seeks buyer for Elk Hills oil.
newsitem.headline: U.S. DOE still seeks buyer for Elk Hills oil.

text.p: The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) said Tuesday it is still looking for buyers for leftover crude oil from its underbid Elk Hills Naval Petroleum Reserve auction in Tupman, Calif..
Around 5,075 barrels-per-day (bpd) of light crude remains to be sold following lower-than-expected demand in last week's government auction.
A DOE official was calling back original buyers, but the three largest winners from last week's auction declined to take any more of the crude.
Four other bidders -- including Texaco Exploration, Paramount Petroleum, U.S. Oil & Refining, and EOTT Energy ETO.N, were possible buyers of the leftover oil.
The DOE said Chevron Corp CHV., a 22 percent stakeholder of Elk Hills, could store some of the slack.
"If there's any left, we can over-deliver their share for a month or two," the DOE official said.
Last Thursday, the DOE received bids for 11,025 barrels of the available 16,100 bpd offered by the government, a low level of demand, according to a DOE official.
The DOE attributed weak demand to heavy volumes of light sweet crude imports, which are forcing more local crude, like Elk Hills grades, into storage.
DOE said Tosco was rumored to be bringing in more foreign crudes this month to test how well they run in the company's newly acquired refineries.
